extraction.name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
extraction.description: A dataset of 7,787 natural grade-school science multiple-choice questions, partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set, released with a 14M-sentence science corpus and baseline models to encourage research in advanced question answering.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation to gather publicly releasable standardized-test science questions from a variety of sources, then partitioned into Challenge and Easy sets based on whether two baseline solvers answered them incorrectly.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Natural science questions authored for standardized tests from a variety of sources; additionally, the ARC Corpus consists of 14M science-related sentences mined from the Web, augmented with the AristoMini corpus.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were partitioned into Challenge and Easy sets using two baseline filters: a retrieval-based IR solver and a PMI word co-occurrence solver. Challenge questions are those answered incorrectly by both solvers.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus, retrieved web documents were de-duplicated, stripped down to text content, and chunked into sentences; the corpus was also augmented with AristoMini.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No new human labeling was created for the questions; grade levels were assigned by the original examiners who authored the questions. The authors also manually categorized sampled Challenge questions by knowledge and reasoning type based on subjective judgment.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper notes that categorization of knowledge and reasoning types is approximate and subjective.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Elasticsearch; proprietary parser plus Open IE; Open IE
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, corpus, baseline models, leaderboard, and up-to-date results are available on the ARC website.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Student grade level / age range (3rd to 9th grade; typically ages 8 through 13)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to redirect QA research toward more difficult reasoning tasks rather than surface-level retrieval, posing a challenge to the community.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper discusses a research bias in prior standardized-test datasets where scores are dominated by simple algorithms, biasing research toward incremental improvements on easy questions; ARC is designed to mitigate this.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Challenge-set definition only approximates hardness; category analyses are subjective; many baseline methods are limited by retrieval bias; the corpus contains relevant knowledge but exploiting it is non-trivial and may still require unstated commonsense knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Advanced question answering research, benchmarking, training/dev/test evaluation, and optional use of the ARC Corpus for solving the Challenge.

description.evidence: We present a new question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering. Together, these constitute the AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)... The dataset contains only natural, grade-school science questions (authored for human tests), and is the largest public-domain set of this kind (7,787 questions). We are also releasing the ARC Corpus, a corpus of 14M science sentences relevant to the task, and implementations of the three neural baseline models tested.
